chapter_title: Improving a Resource with AI Agents
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of ten edited sentences keeps the meaning of the original, and name the kind of change when it does not, with at least 9 of 10 verdicts correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** meaning-preservation-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of ten edited sentences keeps the meaning of the original, and name the kind of change when it does not, with at least 9 of 10 verdicts correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Preserving Original Meaning, Hallucination (both defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 14). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each pair the learner commits Meaning preserved or Meaning changed. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content. When the verdict is Meaning changed, the learner also names the kind of change from the five listed, and the kind is checked in the feedback. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 verdicts correct on the first attempt. Reading the five kinds is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A shorter sentence keeps the same meaning. (2) A small word change is harmless. (3) An edit that adds a true-sounding claim is an improvement. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging whether an edit keeps the author's meaning is an Evaluate-level action that every reviewer of an agent's edits performs. Pairs that include a harmless rewrite and a subtle one teach the learner to compare each qualifier. **Content:** The two verdicts: Meaning preserved, Meaning changed. The five kinds of change: Changed quantity, Changed strength, Dropped qualifier, Added claim, Dropped item. The ten pairs (all made up): | # | Before | After | Correct verdict | Kind of change | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | A watershed is an area of land where all the water drains to the same place. | A watershed is land whose water all drains to one place. | Meaning preserved | None | The claim is the same in fewer words. | | 2 | The Clearwater River drains about 6,000 square miles. | The Clearwater River drains more than 6,000 square miles. | Meaning changed | Changed quantity | "About" became "more than". | | 3 | Most rain soaks into the ground. | Rain soaks into the ground. | Meaning changed | Dropped qualifier | "Most" was dropped, so the claim now covers all rain. | | 4 | Infiltration is the process by which water enters soil. | Infiltration is how water moves into soil. | Meaning preserved | None | The claim is the same in plainer words. | | 5 | Runoff can carry pollutants into the river. | Runoff always carries pollutants into the river. | Meaning changed | Changed strength | "Can" became "always". | | 6 | Wetlands slow the flow of water. | Wetlands slow the flow of water and remove all pollutants. | Meaning changed | Added claim | A new claim was added. | | 7 | Students should record the water level every day for one week. | Students should record the water level daily for a week. | Meaning preserved | None | The instruction is the same. | | 8 | The map shows the river and its tributaries. | The map shows the river. | Meaning changed | Dropped item | The tributaries were dropped. | | 9 | Plants along the bank hold the soil in place. | Plants on the riverbank keep the soil from washing away. | Meaning preserved | None | The claim is the same in other words. | | 10 | Lake Marlow is the largest lake in the watershed. | Lake Marlow is the biggest lake in the watershed. | Meaning preserved | None | "Biggest" and "largest" mean the same here. | **Provenance:** The sentences are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The five kinds of change follow the chapter section "Preserving Original Meaning". **Rules:** Each pair has exactly one correct verdict. Five pairs are Meaning preserved and five are Meaning changed, one for each kind of change. A verdict counts as correct on the verdict alone, and the kind of change is shown as feedback. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one pair, with the changed words not marked. 2. The learner chooses a verdict. If the verdict is Meaning changed, the learner also picks the kind of change. 3. The sim shows whether the verdict was correct, the kind of change, and the Why text, and marks the changed words. 4. After pair 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 pairs in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The meaning was [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can check an edit against the original." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed pair. **Starting State:** The first pair in the shuffled order and the two verdicts. The question shown is "Does the second sentence say the same thing?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists five kinds of edit that change meaning: a changed quantity, a changed strength, a dropped qualifier, an added claim, and a dropped item. Each kind appears once in the pairs.
